title: Afrobeat Beyond the Grammys: Fela Kuti and Contemporary African Creativity
description: Fela Kuti's posthumous Grammy recognition marks a milestone for African innovation. This panel of publicly engaged scholars illuminates the women who shaped his world--from feminist icon Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti to the collaborators and performers who sustained the Afrobeat movement across generations. The event will start with a panel discussion featuring guests Jad Abumrad, Dr. Dotun Ayobade, Kehinde Alonge, and Dr. Judith Byfield. Jad Abumra is the host of the 12-part 2025 podcast series Fela Kuti: Fear No Man, exploring the life of the Afrobeat pioneer. Afterwards, there will be a reception with live music played by DJ AK-47. Co-Sponsored by the Center for African Studies, English Department, Women and Gender Studies, and AMESALL. Come learn and socialize in the Livingston Student Center Gathering Lounge!

title: GESA Qualifying Exam Roundtable
description: Having trouble balancing day-to-day studies with preparations for the qualifying exams this spring? We'd love to help with that in any way that we can. One of our annual traditions with GESA is hosting a “roundtable” (like a presenter panel, but much more informal) event to talk about these exams and some things that we have learned from it, as upper-level students who have gone through the experience just like all of you. So we invite you to attend and to come chat with us! See below for the event details. — WHEN: Tuesday, March 24, 5:00 - 7:00 PM WHERE: Simon Library (3rd floor), New Jersey Hall WHAT: This event is hosted for the express purpose of giving all students taking the qualifiers a chance to have an open and honest dialogue with a mixture of upper-level students. Our goal is to help you feel more prepared as you decide which exams to take, and also as you decide how you want to prepare for the summer. Importantly, GESA will be providing FREE FOOD to all attendees!

title: Needlepoint Workshop with artist Liz Collins

description: Join the Center for Women in the Arts at Douglass for a workshop led by acclaimed artist Liz Collins! This unique needlepoint workshop invites you to explore the meditative joy of stitching. Collins will guide participants through the myriad of stitches possible within needlepoint and share her distinctive methodology for creating improvisational designs, treating needlepoint as a slow drawing process in response to the grid. All skill levels and forms of stitching are welcome and supported. Only open to Douglass and Art & Design students. Free supplies and snacks provided! Supplies/snacks are limited – First come, first served. Space is limited. Please arrive on-time. This experience counts towards the Douglass Discovery curriculum requirement. R3: Career/Discovery/Professional Development/Research. Reminder: To receive DRC curriculum credit, you must complete a reflection survey . *Liz Collins is the 2025-2026 Estelle Lebowitz & Ann Beneduce-Lebowitz Artist-in-Residence. Her solo exhibition, Shapeshifter , is on view through March 13, 2026 in the Mary H. Dana Women Artists Series Galleries at Douglass Libraries. ___ * Image and Media Release By attending this event, you acknowledge and agree that Rutgers University may photograph, record, or otherwise capture your artwork, image, and/or voice. title: Mass
description: Join us for the Rutgers University Student Mass at 6:00 PM on Sundays in St. Peter the Apostle Church, located on College Avenue next to Barnes & Noble. The Mass, or Celebration of the Eucharist, is the central act of worship in the Catholic tradition, in which Christ’s sacrifice on the Cross is made present, and the faithful are united to Him through the proclamation of the Word and the reception of Holy Communion. It is both a sacrifice and a sacred meal, instituted by Jesus at the Last Supper. All are welcome! There'll be a free dinner in the Catholic Center afterwards :)

title: STD Awareness and Prevention with Service Event
club_name: Rutgers University Latino Medical Student Association Pre-Health Latino Undergraduate Society
description: A discussion about awareness, prevention, and staying informed. Join us for an engaging panel event focused on important conversations around STDs followed with a service event by making AIDS awareness pins! This event will also kick off our fundraising efforts in preparation for the AIDs Walk, so come out, learn, and support a meaningful cause.

title: Rubik's Cube Club General Meeting!
description: Learn to solve the Rubik's Cube for the first time or expand your speedcubing knowledge and skills!
